neighbours.label: Abstract nouns for what people hold in common in talk of human relations: 'knowledge' / 'interests' after 'mutual', 'shared' or 'common' (weak, mostly gate-closed pole)
fire: Good neighbours come to rely on mutual knowledge and common interests built up over years.
The two tribes kept the peace through shared knowledge of each other's customs.
A lasting marriage grows out of mutual knowledge rather than sudden passion.
Grandparents and children can discover common interests that bring them closer.
The club was founded so that members with shared interests and mutual knowledge could meet.
Trust between colleagues depends on mutual knowledge of one another's habits.
Old rivals sometimes find that common interests and shared knowledge outweigh their quarrels.
The friendship rested on mutual knowledge gained during long years at sea.
quiet: Good neighbours come to borrow tools and return them late over the years.
The two tribes kept the peace by trading salt for dried fish.
A lasting marriage needs patience rather than sudden passion.
Grandparents and children can bake bread together on rainy days.
The club was founded so that members could play chess on Fridays.
Quarrels between colleagues often start over small things like parking.
Old rivals sometimes shake hands and forget their quarrels.
The friendship began on a fishing boat during a long storm at sea.

notes: Card flags gate-closed regime (-x- echo 90%); peaks ' mutual', 'interested', ' will', ' knowledge'. Probes were weak: 'mutual knowledge … common interests' 0.24, 'shared knowledge of each other' 0.25, 'mutual interests' 0.19, 'our wills' 0.14; unrelated sentences sit at about 0.05-0.10. Likely to miss the 0.20 median.
